intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that atrial standstill-1 (ATRST1) can be caused by mutation in the SCN5A gene (600163) on chromosome 3p22.2 occurring together with rare polymorphisms in the connexin-40 gene GJA5 (121013) on chromosome 1q21.2, consistent with digenic inheritance.

checks.claim: Atrial standstill-1 (ATRST1) can be caused by mutation in the SCN5A gene occurring together with rare polymorphisms in the connexin-40 gene GJA5.
checks.evidence_quote: In this study, familial AS was associated with the concurrence of a cardiac sodium channel mutation and rare polymorphisms in the atrial-specific Cx40 gene.
checks.explanation: The paper reports an association and proposes that the combined genetic changes lead to atrial standstill. Cx40 is GJA5.

checks.claim: The SCN5A gene is located on chromosome 3p22.2.
checks.evidence_quote: novel mutation in the cardiac sodium channel gene SCN5A (D1275N)
checks.explanation: The chromosomal location is standard nomenclature that is not stated in the paper but is acceptable as a restatement of the gene.

checks.claim: The GJA5 gene is located on chromosome 1q21.2.
checks.evidence_quote: the gene for the atrial-specific gap junction protein connexin40 (Cx40)
checks.explanation: The chromosomal location is standard nomenclature that is not stated in the paper but is acceptable as a restatement of the gene.

checks.claim: The co-occurrence of an SCN5A mutation with rare GJA5 polymorphisms in atrial standstill-1 is consistent with digenic inheritance.
checks.evidence_quote: The three living AS patients exclusively coinherited both the rare Cx40 genotype and the SCN5A-D1275N mutation.
checks.explanation: The word 'digenic' is not used, but the paper reports that changes in two genes were coinherited and acted together, which amounts to digenic inheritance.

paragraphs.text: Atrial standstill is a rare arrhythmia (Groenewegen et al., 2003). In a family with the disorder, Groenewegen et al. (2003) found that atrial standstill was associated with a mutation in the cardiac sodium channel gene SCN5A occurring together with rare polymorphisms in the atrial-specific gap junction gene GJA5 (connexin-40).

paragraphs.text: The findings of Groenewegen et al. (2003) suggested digenic inheritance of familial atrial standstill. In the family they studied, the 3 affected living patients were the only members who coinherited both the SCN5A mutation and a rare GJA5 (connexin-40) genotype. The SCN5A mutation was also present in 5 unaffected relatives.

checks.claim: The findings of Groenewegen et al. (2003) suggested digenic inheritance of familial atrial standstill.
checks.evidence_quote: We propose that, although the functional effect of each genetic change is relatively benign, the combined effect of genetic changes eventually progresses to total AS.
checks.explanation: The paper proposes that changes in two genes act together to cause the disorder, which implies digenic inheritance.

paragraphs.text: Groenewegen et al. (2003) used candidate gene screening in a family with atrial standstill. They identified an asp1275-to-asn (D1275N) mutation in the SCN5A gene in all 3 affected living relatives. The affected patients coinherited the mutation with a rare genotype of 2 closely linked polymorphisms in regulatory regions of the connexin-40 gene (GJA5). In functional studies, D1275N channels showed a small depolarizing shift in activation compared with wildtype channels. The authors proposed that, although each genetic change had a relatively benign functional effect, their combined effect eventually progressed to total atrial standstill.

paragraphs.text: Makita et al. (2005) identified a novel SCN5A mutation in a family with atrial standstill. The affected proband carried both the SCN5A mutation and connexin-40 polymorphisms. Makita et al. (2005) noted that incomplete penetrance in atrial standstill had been attributed in part to digenic inheritance of connexin-40 polymorphisms together with an SCN5A mutation.

checks.claim: Makita et al. (2005) identified a novel SCN5A mutation in a family with atrial standstill.
checks.evidence_quote: The novel SCN5A mutation L212P was identified in the proband (age 11 years) and his father.

checks.claim: The affected proband of the atrial standstill family studied by Makita et al. (2005) carried both the novel SCN5A mutation and connexin-40 polymorphisms.
checks.evidence_quote: Further screenings for genetic variations that might mitigate L212P dysfunction revealed that the proband, but not his father, carries Cx40 polymorphisms inherited from his asymptomatic mother.
checks.explanation: The proband carries both L212P and the Cx40 polymorphisms.

checks.claim: Makita et al. (2005) noted that incomplete penetrance in atrial standstill had been attributed in part to digenic inheritance of connexin-40 polymorphisms together with an SCN5A mutation.
checks.evidence_quote: Incomplete penetrance observed in atrial standstill has been attributed in part to the digenic inheritance of polymorphisms in the atrial-specific gap junction connexin 40 (Cx40) in conjunction with an SCN5A mutation.
